decision: Coder views show request, response, editor and next actions uncut. The standard 8,000-character cap is not used in Bet 4
why: Standard cap cuts 8 next-action blocks and 1 response character in the sample. 7 of those windows could hide uptake evidence: later edits after a matched paste, a 30+ character run shared with the response, or further pastes (scripts/truncation.py)
effect: 0 main blocks cut in coder views. Coders read about 733,000 characters. View size per coder batch stays near Bet 3's

decision: Earlier turns stay cut at 500 characters, except an earlier AI response whose cut part shares a 30+ character run with this request or editor is shown whole
why: Earlier turns are context, and whole earlier turns would add about 200,000 characters. 139 of 274 earlier blocks are cut, and a request that reuses earlier AI text changes prior_own_work and the origin step of decision
effect: 19 windows see at least one earlier response whole. Older turns outside the 3 shown remain unseen

decision: Script overlap is not shown to coders. It runs after labeling, as v1.1 s7 says
why: Codebook is frozen and says coders do not see these numbers. With no cut left, nothing needs a script stand-in for unread text
effect: Audit reported per window in results/

decision: A gold window is marked as less complete on the Fable page if (a) a next-action block was cut there and the cut is uptake-material under truncation.py, or (b) an earlier AI response reused by the request or editor was cut there. Written before Fable labels were opened
why: The brief asks to mark windows rather than rerun. The test should not be chosen after seeing labels
effect: Marks NIRVANA-e27-t02 under (a); NIRVANA-e26-t11, NIRVANA-e70-t07 and WILDCHAT-0685972d7031-t03 under (b)

decision: Each coder is 5 fresh same-model subagents, one per batch of 16 to 23 windows, sessions kept whole
why: 100 uncut windows are about 5 times a Bet 3 round. One agent would overflow or compact mid-run. Bet 3 coders read 145 KB per round; batches are 145 to 148 KB
effect: Within-coder drift across batches is not measured

decision: One text file per window, lines wrapped at 200 characters, each ending in an end marker
why: Reading tools can drop long lines or large files
effect: Line breaks can split a run, which matters little since overlap runs on raw text

decision: Requested models: opus for Coder A, sonnet for Coder B, as in Bet 3. Transcripts recorded the served model: claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5
why: Numbers should compare with Bet 3, whose served model was not recorded
effect: Temperature still cannot be set. Sets of runs are not repeatable, so labels are saved

decision: Coder separation is checked from transcripts by path: no other-coder, Fable, pilot, data or results path in any tool call, and every line of each view returned to its coder
why: Bet 3 had separation by instruction only. The audit's first regex hit coder_brief.md and tool-results, so it was fixed and rerun
effect: 0 violations in 10 agents. Coder A batch 4 listed blind/ once, which shows folder names only, and made scratch copies of its own views, then deleted them

decision: Adjudicator requested as opus, one fresh agent. Labels shown as first and second with a seeded per-window flip, with both coders' notes
why: Opus is also Coder A's model, so the flip hides which is which. Fable is excluded so the third check stays separate
effect: The rate of siding with each coder is reported, since same-model preference cannot be fully hidden

decision: The one field the adjudicator did not settle stays UNSETTLED in final_labels.csv (NIRVANA-e06-t02 verification, coders V2 and V0). Bet 5 excludes it or runs both readings
why: The brief says flag instead of force. The written s6 rules leave open a criterion handed to the AI with no failing asserted
effect: 99 of 100 windows have a final verification code

decision: The script rule of v1.1 s7 was applied after adjudication: U1 vs U2 goes to the script. No override was needed
why: All 11 U1 and U2 labels with a script reading already matched it

decision: NIRVANA-e56-t01 keeps U3 although the script finds no 30+ character run. Only U1 vs U2 is the script's to settle
why: v1.1 gives the script no authority on U3. The window is listed as an audit flag

why: The brief asks to mark, not rerun
effect: Leaving them out moves decision k from 0.84 to 0.88 and uptake k from 0.81 to 0.84
